# Persian Studies Minor
Source: https://academiccatalog.umd.edu/undergraduate/colleges-schools/arts-humanities/languages-literatures-cultures/persian-studies/persian-studies-minor/
Source: https://sllc.umd.edu/persian
Source: https://arhu.umd.edu/academics/undergraduate-studies/minors
Fetched: 2026-09-28

## Catalog requirements

Course | Title | Credits
Core Language Sequence (12 credits)
PERS103 | Beginning Persian I (Beginning Persian I) | 3
PERS104 | Beginning Persian II (Beginning Persian II) | 3
PERS201 | Intermediate Persian I | 3
PERS202 | Intermediate Persian II | 3
Electives (Choose 9 credits) | 9
PERS353 | Iranian Life in Literature and Film
PERS371 | Introduction to Persian Literature in Translation
PERS385 | Theatre and Dance in Iran and Afghanistan
PERS498 | Special Topics in Persian Studies
Total Credits | 21
No prerequisites are required for students with equivalent knowledge. Placement assessment is mandatory. (https://arhu.umd.edu/academics/foreign-language-placement/online-flpa)
Once credits have been received for a higher-level language focus course, a lower-level course may not be taken for credit (For example, PERS201 may not be taken after PERS202).
Up to 6 approved credits transferred from other institutions can count toward language requirements for the minor (see https://registrar.umd.edu/transfer-credit).
Students placing out of language courses due to prior proficiency must complete substitute courses in consultation with the Undergraduate Advisor.
Electives may be substituted in consultation with the Undergraduate Advisor.
Courses may not be used to fulfill the requirements of two minors.
At least 9 credits must be taken at the upper-level (courses numbered 300 or above).
All courses presented for the minor must be passed with a grade of "C-" or better.
An overall GPA of 2.0 in the minor is required for graduation.

Prospective Students
Persian Studies Academic Programs
Undergraduate students can pursue a B.A. in Persian studies or a minor in Persian studies. Students wishing to achieve advanced proficiency in Persian should also consider the Flagship Scholar Certificate through the University's Persian Language Flagship Program. This certificate can be combined with many other majors. Graduate students can apply for the new M.P.S. in Persian and explore additional opportunities for graduate study in Persian, including at the Ph.D. level.

About the Persian Program
The Persian program offers a B.A. and a minor for undergraduate students and an M.P.S. in Persian for graduate students, and remains committed to providing a diverse, rigorous curriculum that offers students the opportunity to achieve a high level of proficiency in the Persian language as well as attain a broader understanding of Persian culture, history, art and literature.
Graduate students also have the opportunity to explore an education in Persian at the Ph.D. level through partnerships with various departments and in collaboration with the Graduate School.

Undergraduate Studies
Minors are an excellent way for students to gain expertise in an area beyond the major. We encourage students to work with their advisors early to incorporate the minor into their Academic Plans.
Applications for all minors remain open until the minor is filled. Students will be taken on a first-come, first-served basis. When you click on the “contact form” below and select the appropriate option on the form, your request will be marked with the date and time. Please keep in mind that any pre-requisites must be completed by the time of application. (Students applying to the Music Performance minor must successfully pass an audition and should contact the advisor through the form below as soon as possible.)
When a minor is listed as CLOSED, it is closed until October 1 in the fall semester or March 1 in the spring semester. You may check this site again at these times. When a minor is listed as WAITLIST, it is closed, but you may put yourself on a waitlist by clicking on "contact form" below and selecting the appropriate option.
